details: Migration 014 marker is installed.
Guest-token lifecycle trigger is attached to public.guest_sessions.
A new active stay receives its first signed token.
Hotel, room, guest and expiry changes explicitly rotate access.
An unrelated guest-session update cannot silently reactivate revoked access.
Inactive, checked-out and expired stays invalidate active tokens.
The staff QR response separates stay status from access status.
Automatic recovery is limited to active legacy stays with no token history.
Refreshing link administration preserves manual revocation.
Only an active and unexpired token is rendered into guest URLs.
Explicit rotation revokes the previous active token before issuance.
The database permits at most one active token per guest stay.
Revoked and expired token records cannot resolve.
Checkout and stay expiry invalidate previously signed URLs.
Rendered access uses UUID nonce plus SHA-256 HMAC signature.
Malformed or altered signatures are rejected by the resolver.
A signed token is bound to its hotel slug.
The resolver accepts signed UUID-plus-HMAC tokens, never room numbers.
Raw tokens and signing secrets are not exposed to browser roles.
Only authenticated hotel staff can administer secure guest links.
Anonymous access remains restricted to approved RPCs.
Every public table carrying hotel_id has RLS enabled.
Every token remains bound to one hotel, room and authoritative stay.
Both StayQR Storage buckets are private and have all eight policies.
